candidate_adjudication.source_mapping: RCSB title identifies CaMKII-alpha kinase domain with GluN2B(S1303D), but the detected ATP donor is associated with the GluN2B chain and the closest hydroxyl is CaMKII Thr176, not a source-mapped substrate acceptor.
RCSB title identifies cyanobacterial circadian clock protein KaiC; this is not a source-mapped ePK substrate-transfer complex despite EC 2.7.11-like annotation and cross-chain ATP/Mg-to-Thr geometry.

candidate_adjudication.summary: ATM(Q2971A) Mg AMP-PNP sibling structures from the same oxidative-stress activation paper lack the modeled p53 peptide and have no heteromeric acceptor hit.

evidence_against: The start=100 canonical page found no fresh folded-protein ePK positive. Fresh positives are synthetic peptide contexts.
7KL1 is a wrong-associated-donor counterexample: ATP is associated with GluN2B while the closest acceptor is CaMKII Thr176.
7V3X is an out-of-scope KaiC clock autokinase-style counterexample, not a clean ePK kinase-substrate complex.
ATM siblings 8OXP and 8OXQ have Mg AMP-PNP but no p53 peptide/substrate acceptor.
evidence_for: Fresh review-only ATM/p53 peptide positives: 8OXM and 8OXO source-map p53 Ser15 near ANP PG with local Mg in Mg AMP-PNP structures.
source_review_summary.recommendation: Use 8OXM and 8OXO only as review-only peptide positive evidence. Keep production scoring, threshold calibration, label imports, registries, fingerprints, migrations, and production claims closed.
